card.name: Musette (bal-musette)
card.era: From the 1880s in Paris; peak to 1945; decline ~1960; revival since
card.profile: Bal-musette is a style of French popular music and dance that became popular in Paris from the 1880s, centered on the accordion and the working-class dance halls of the Bastille (rue de Lappe) and the guinguettes (Wikipedia). Auvergnat immigrants first danced the bourree to the cabrette bagpipe (locally 'musette') and hurdy-gurdy; Italian immigrant accordionists later transformed the scene, the accordion displacing the bagpipe. Its repertoire of close-embrace 'musette-form' dances includes the valse-musette (with the toupie variation), tango-musette, paso-musette, polka, mazurka and the java. Performers include Antoine Bouscatel, Emile Vacher, Charles Peguri and Gus Viseur; the 1930s saw cross-pollination with Django Reinhardt's gypsy jazz.
card.insight: More a scene/style than a single dance - by 1945 it was the most popular style of dance in France before declining sharply around 1960 (Wikipedia).
